text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German debt was trading slightly higher but down from intra-day highs near the session-end as traders said the market was becoming infected with a traditional year-end lethargy often seen this time of the year.
The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.20, up 0.13 from Friday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - Gilts ended little changed, unable to cling on to the higher ground they charted in early trade and bracing for a wave of statistics through the rest of the week.
The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-02/32, up 01/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled higher amid hopes that the so-called European Union "stability pact" deal struck late on Friday will give the Bank of France room to lower interest rates, possibly before the end of the year.
The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.46, down 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to firmer levels helped by an early boost from a European stability pact and support from many other bond markets but the market showed nervousness at the higher levels, dealers said.
The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.82, up 0.40 from Friday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened higher in light trade after a mild buying spree in Tokyo and London prompted some follow-through purchases in New York early morning trade, analysts said.
The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-04/32, down 04/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.60 percent.
JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher in quiet trade, after being boosted in the morning by a rise in U.S. Treasuries on Friday.
In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 125.27, up 0.12 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - The Eurobond market entered its quietest period of the year without even a whimper, recording no new issues of any note.

While further league table-related activity and a few small structured deals from LatAm borrowers were expected later in the week, mainstream primary market business will remain at a virtual standstill until after the year-end break.

Then, as ever in early January, heavy issuance will hit the market, causing new year bullishness to turn to talk of oversupplied markets inside a fortnight, dealers said. Last week's activity brought the volume of international bonds launched this year to around $665 billion, $200 billion more than last year's record-breaking total.
